thread:
sam_devex: Heads up — found a mismatch between the new policy gating header and SDKs. TS and Python default to dropping/serializing unknown shapes, so some canary traffic is getting quota attribution regressions.

maria_platform: Ugh. Which header shape are we sending? paste sample pls

sam_devex: Example we pushed: `x-rd-route-policy: {"policy":"cost-optimized","quota_key":"cc-123"}` — server expects a single string token. Some SDKs stringify differently or coerce to `[object Object]`.

alex_ts_sdk: Confirmed. TS SDK's `headerSerializer` does `String(value)` for non-strings which yields `[object Object]` and policy-service rejects.

ryan_py_sdk: Python behavior is inconsistent: requests will send dicts as json bodies if used that way, but we were setting headers via a map so we end up sending the repr which varies by caller.

lee_eng: How widespread? Any telemetry showing failures? cc: @ci-bot

ci-bot: Canary metrics for last 24h: 4.1% of requests to policy endpoint returning 400 with `invalid-header` in eu-west-1 cluster.

maria_platform: Proposed plan: 1) SDK patches to normalize header to a deterministic string (e.g., base64(JSON)) and emit a `policy_header_normalized` event; 2) Policy-service support both stringified JSON and encoded string for 30 days; 3) Console telemetry tile to surface normalized vs raw rates and a deprecation banner.

jordan_product: UX note — console shouldn't alarm users for this during rollout. We should surface a non-blocking banner + toggle to enable strict mode per account. Also prep customer comms for those who rely on quota attribution.

natalie_devex: Docs/workflow: I'll draft migration examples for Python, TS, and Go. Want minimal code snippets and a note about opting in to strict mode later.

alex_ts_sdk: I can ship a non-breaking TS patch (1.2.1) that normalizes and adds an opt-in env flag `RD_POLICY_STRICT=false` by default. Then we flip in 2.0. Will include a unit test and an e2e sandbox test.

ryan_py_sdk: I'll prepare a Python 0.9.x patch that marshals header to JSON then base64-encodes it. Add telemetry event and a small migration guide.

lee_eng: Also please add server-side logging that hashes the raw header (no PII) and stores sampling at 0.5% for debugging. Telemetry team: okay with sampling and hashing?

maria_platform: Telemetry OK if hashed and rate-limited. We'll default sampling to 0.5% and allow increasing for specific orgs under support.

sam_devex: Can we avoid breaking customers mid-rollout? Suggest server accepts both formats for 30 days and emits a deprecation warning in response header `x-rd-policy-deprecated: true`.

jordan_product: Agree — also craft a short in-console banner + a targeted email to customers whose quota attribution changed >5% in last 7 days.

alex_ts_sdk: Timeline proposal: TS patch today -> canary release tomorrow; Python patch today -> release in 48h. Server change to accept both landed tonight; then telemetry + console tile next week.

natalie_devex: I'll draft banner copy now, open docs PR, and add migration code snippets.

lee_eng: Adding canary metrics dashboard: https://console.redwood.internal/canary/policy-header (will share perms).

sam_devex: Action items recap: alex -> TS PR and release; ryan -> Py PR and release; lee -> policy-service acceptance + hashing; natalie -> docs + banner; maria -> telemetry sampling config + console tile; jordan -> customer comms plan.

alex_ts_sdk: PR will reference this thread, pinging @ryan_py_sdk for cross-tests.

ryan_py_sdk: On it. I'll add unit tests and a small e2e against sandbox with canary header shapes.

maria_platform: Thanks everyone — sync in morning stand if any blocker.

jordan_product: Thx all :thumbsup:
